podcast.title: Accidental Simply Red Stage Invasion
podcast.body: One day, due to being heavily intoxicated, Shaun Ryder overslept and missed his bandmates and roadies departing for a gig. Rushing to the venue, he mistakenly ran onto the stage of Simply Red, who were performing a few doors down, believing it was the Happy Mondays' stage. "Unfortunately, he went into the wrong place. He accidentally invaded the stage of simply red. The Mondays were playing a few doors down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Crack Consumption During Recording
podcast.body: During the recording sessions for the Happy Mondays' fourth album in Barbados, Shaun Ryder reportedly spent up to 20 hours a day in the bathroom smoking crack. "It said that Sean spent up to 20 hours in the bathroom smoking crack during those sessions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Postman Bites Dog Incident
podcast.body: As a postman, finding his job boring, Shaun Ryder took a tab of acid on his rounds. When a territorial terrier attacked him at a pub where he was dropping off mail, Ryder picked up the dog and bit it, leading to his suspension after another postman reported him. "He picked up the dog and bit it. Another postman going by saw this, reported him, and he was suspended."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Manchester Pigeon Massacre
podcast.body: Growing up in Manchester, Shaun Ryder harbored a strong dislike for pigeons. After an incident where birds tried to steal his Kentucky Fried Chicken, he exacted revenge, claiming to have caused about 3,000 pigeons to fall from the sky over Manchester through conflicting methods such as feeding them rat poison or tiny rocks of crack, meth, or ecstasy. "Anyway, by the time he was done, Sean says that about 3,000 pigeons fell from the sky over Manchester."

xref.title: Barbados Recording Session Chaos - Shaun Ryder Crashes into Bar
xref.body: One night, while Gazz Wheeling was drinking at a small, shack-like bar, Shaun Ryder drove a car straight through the front of the establishment, asking for Gazz. The bar owner, a former West Indian cricketer, was wealthy and calmly stated he would pay for the damage, as did the band. "This car comes through the front, the front bit of the bar... And everyone jumped up and then show mocks instead of heard you was here."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Conflict with Noel Gallagher
xref.body: Noel Gallagher, who later rose to fame with Oasis, had a past "fall out with Sean" (presumably Shaun Ryder, or a member of Inspiral Carpets named Sean) because "Sean had some words in his spirals," indicating a disagreement or conflict involving the band. "He'd fallen out with Sean because Sean had some words in his spirals."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Control Room Couch Traded for Drugs
xref.body: During the recording of their fourth album in Barbados, singer Shaun Ryder and Bez famously traded the control room couch from the studio for drugs. "And the couch from the control room at the studio disappeared because Sean and Bez traded it for drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Interactions with Happy Mondays
xref.body: Gazz Wheeling and Kelly knew Noel Gallagher personally. Gazz recalls interviewing him "for a few drinks" in a downstairs area, noting a past conflict where Noel "had fallen out with Sean" (likely Shaun Ryder or a member of Inspiral Carpets) due to "words in his spirals." During this early interaction, Noel even offered to play drums for Happy Mondays if they ever needed someone. "He said, if you ever need anyone to do your drums, I'll do it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Gazz Wheeling's Departure
xref.body: Gazz Wheeling decided to leave the Happy Mondays after a tour in Australia because Shaun Ryder was cutting set times to as little as 20 minutes, despite headlining festivals requiring 90-minute sets, and expecting to be paid to record new music. Wheeling felt Shaun Ryder was doing "what he wanted to do," and there was mutual fatigue among the members. "Sean, you know, was cutting the set, so he wanted to do 20 minutes... he'd pay me to come in the studio to do recordings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Relationship with Noel Gallagher
xref.body: Gazz Wheeling recalls Noel Gallagher having a falling out with Shaun Ryder but maintaining a good relationship with Clint Boon, The Charlatans' keyboard player, through whom Gazz and his wife Kelly knew Noel. "he'd fallen out with Sean because Sean had some words in his barrels, but I hadn't, because I knew Clint was okay. And me and, and Kelly knew Noll through him."

xref.title: Reunions Not for Tax Reasons
xref.body: Shaun Ryder claimed the band reunited multiple times for tax reasons, but Gazz Wheeling stated this was a "safety net" to avoid appearing as if they genuinely wanted or needed to reunite, reflecting a "Mancunian" attitude of not showing enjoyment for commercial endeavors. "No, that was, that was just Sean saying that to kind of, ever, as a bit of a, a, a safety net in case it all went perjokes, just so it looked like we, the thing, well, it's kind of like not trying to look like we needed to get back all we wanted to."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Oral History of Manchester Part 2

xref.title: Reunions and Shaun Ryder's Persona
xref.body: The Happy Mondays reunited only once after an initial break, not multiple times for "tax reasons" as sometimes suggested. Gazz Wheeling clarified that Shaun Ryder used the "tax reasons" excuse as a "safety net" to maintain a "real Manchester finger" persona, where not "enjoying it" was considered "cool" and a reflection of a working-class English identity. "No, that was, that was just Sean saying that to kind of ever, as a bit of a, a safety net in case it all went pear-shaped."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shaun Ryder's Shyness and Insecurity
xref.body: Despite his wild public persona, Shaun Ryder is described as being "shy" and "insecure." This hidden shyness, combined with the band's collective insecurities, was suggested to be a driving force behind some of their behavior, rooted in a working-class English mentality of "not getting above your station." "No, Sean was kind of, a little more Sean, yeah, it's shy, Sean, shy. So that's why he did it, you know, he was shy, basically, and we were kind of all kind of insecure."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shaun Ryder's Unconventional Recording Process
xref.body: Shaun Ryder typically did not get involved in the music composition, preferring to add lyrics later, often after the music for an entire album was written. For "Yes Please," he only contributed lyrics for one song, which was unusual even for his late-stage lyric writing habits. "he'd always did the lyrics later, he never got involved in the music, ever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
